China Ever Grand Financial Leasing Group Co., Ltd. ( (HK:0379) ) just unveiled an update.

China Ever Grand Financial Leasing Group Co., Ltd. reported unaudited interim results for the six months ended 30 June 2026, reflecting a notable turnaround in profitability. The group operates in financial leasing and related services, with revenue streams from customer contracts, leases and interest income, complemented by returns from equity investments and associates.

For the current period, total revenue rose to HK$61.1 million from HK$39.9 million a year earlier, but gross profit slipped to HK$6.5 million due to higher cost of revenue. The company nevertheless swung to a profit attributable to shareholders of HK$45.5 million from a loss of HK$37.7 million, driven mainly by a HK$54.5 million gain on disposal of subsidiaries and a positive HK$4.6 million share of results of associates.

Other comprehensive income surged to HK$91.5 million, largely on substantial fair value gains of HK$87.1 million on equity investments measured at FVTOCI. As a result, total comprehensive income attributable to owners jumped to HK$137.0 million from a loss of HK$28.5 million in the prior-year period, boosting earnings per share to 2.70 Hong Kong cents from a loss per share of 2.23 Hong Kong cents.

The improvement in associate performance and the disposal of subsidiaries significantly strengthened the group’s bottom line, despite continued administrative expenses and increased expected credit loss provisions. The strong uplift in fair value of equity holdings also enhanced the group’s balance sheet position, with the interim results suggesting a recovery in financial performance that may support investor confidence if these gains prove sustainable.

Gossamer Bio ( (GOSS) ) has shared an announcement.

On August 20, 2026, Gossamer Bio entered into a structured private placement of up to approximately $250 million, built around milestone-based pre-funded and approval-linked warrants to finance seralutinib’s path through U.S. regulatory review for pulmonary arterial hypertension. The deal, publicly announced on August 21, 2026, includes $150 million of committed capital, with $25 million expected at an initial closing on August 24, 2026 and $125 million upon FDA acceptance of the seralutinib NDA, plus up to $100 million from warrants exercisable only after FDA approval.

The financing, which features non-voting convertible preferred stock, lock-up provisions, beneficial ownership limits and a requirement for Nasdaq-mandated stockholder approval before common shares can be issued, brings in leading healthcare investors and existing shareholders to back Gossamer’s pulmonary hypertension franchise. Proceeds from the initial and second closings, combined with current cash reserves, are expected to fund operations into 2028 and support late-stage development and potential commercialization of seralutinib in PAH and PH-ILD, while leaving the ultimate level and timing of shareholder dilution dependent on future regulatory outcomes and warrant exercises.
